quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Red flashing lights and gates are present and working.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger or stop sign tells you to stop. Also stop if you see red flashing lights and gates that are working.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving after drinking alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking. It puts you and others on the road at risk.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you while driving in the District of Columbia, you must provide your valid driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.
questions.explanation: You must give the police officer your valid driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. If you do not, you may be fined or arrested.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes to warn other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: A school bus stopped in front of you has red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must have the right-of-way at all times.

questions.question: A school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing. You must:

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights and a stop arm, you must stop. Do not move until the red lights stop and the stop arm goes back. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two-way traffic is ahead.

questions.question: A sign that someone may be driving drunk is:

options.text: They are driving slower than normal traffic.
They are making quick and sudden stops.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction traffic must go on that street. It shows which way you must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but it harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance. It makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: What can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave extra time for your trip.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not following traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not following traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.
Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.
Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, check that your tires have good tread and the right air pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" can result from:

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop paying attention to traffic around you. This makes it easy to miss vehicles that are slowing down or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: Is it permitted to drive under the influence of any medication that impairs your driving?

options.text: If it is prescribed by a physician.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription and over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signals. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. You must focus all your attention on driving. Any other activity is dangerous.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Tired driving is as dangerous as drunk driving. If you feel tired, stop driving right away.

questions.question: What does a "No passing zone" sign mean?

options.text: It is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other cars in that area. These signs are used in places where you cannot see far ahead, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: What should you do if you are getting tired while driving?

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take a break every hour on long trips. If possible, take turns driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: What is this bicyclist signaling?
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead. A straight left arm means they are turning left.
